episode_thesis: Doug King argues that commodities are cyclical because innovation and substitution (shale, GMO) end each scarcity story, so a bottom-up fundamental approach that checks the physical cash market before trading futures is the way to catch rare distortions, using curve trades when imbalances are temporary. He controls risk with a roughly 21% volatility target cut in staged fashion after losses, and warns that the last leg of spikes is margin-call stress rather than fundamentals.

speakers.name: Doug King
speakers.role: Founder of Merchant Commodity Fund (since 2004); former Cargill global head of petroleum trading; owner of Coventry City FC
speakers.speaker_note: Captions spell him 'Duck King' and host 'Morett Sebert'; clear two-speaker interview. Fund returns (60% in 2014) are self-reported.

worldview_premises.premise: Commodities are cyclical, not secularly rising, because innovation and substitution end each scarcity story (shale, GMO seeds).
worldview_premises.support: Oil at $55 in 2025 vs $50 in 2005; shale added about 9 million b/d in 15 years; $150-200 forecasts of 2007-08 failed; grains resilient to weather.

worldview_premises.premise: Buy-and-hold passive commodity exposure loses money.
worldview_premises.support: USO and UNG static-roll ETFs lost everything, USO especially when WTI went negative.

worldview_premises.premise: Physical-market information (basis, cash market) is the key input; futures prices can diverge from cash and give conviction signals.
worldview_premises.support: Career at Cargill; copper 2024 example; takes information only from physical participants.

worldview_premises.premise: Precious metals are not driven by physical supply and demand and are excluded from the universe.
Edge is filtering relevant from irrelevant information; too granular tracking (ships, tank tops) misses the bigger picture.
Trading houses use physical information to trade leveraged derivatives, which pays in distortions such as 2021-22.
Rare distortions deliver the bulk of returns, so one must be positioned in advance; entering after the move is late.
worldview_premises.support: Advice given to investors; no data.

worldview_premises.premise: The last stage of a spike (cocoa, coffee, WTI negative, cotton) is margin-call stress, not fundamentals; exchange margin and limit rules shape moves.
worldview_premises.support: Cocoa, coffee, cotton merchant, 2007-09 limit-down episodes.

worldview_premises.premise: Exchanges may intervene in extreme squeezes (LME nickel cancelled trades), so there is exchange-intervention risk.
Losing money is very poor because cutting the volatility target after a loss slows recovery; the hardest job is to make money the right way.
Independent positioning against the crowd, e.g. bearish at peak oil sentiment, is right.
A merchant's fundamental view had an edge in 2004 when Asia was booming and few vehicles offered commodity exposure.

mechanism_chains.topic: Margin stress squeezes shorts and hedgers

steps.from: Exchange raises margins near the highs (cocoa)
steps.to: Shorts with 20% higher holding cost cover the next day
Margin calls drive them out even though their book is hedged
Final stage is financial stress, not real demand

decision_process.practice: Oil, gas, industrial metals and softs; no precious metals.
Bottom-up supply-demand work with cash-versus-futures divergence for conviction; optimisation and timing tools only for execution.
Takes information from the physical industry, not derivative sellers; weighs others' views against physical facts; took physical delivery (rubber, raw sugar) to test scarcity.
Demand stress tests and deep theoretical work rather than tracking ships or tank tops.
decision_process.why: Too granular misses the main point.

decision_process.practice: 5-20 strategies in 2-4 themes with limits per theme; concentrated but not all-in.
Sectors can sit idle for years when no supply-demand story gives a risk-reward (grains 2017-19).
decision_process.why: Do not waste risk on no story.

decision_process.practice: Volatility target about 21% annualised; no more than half of that when out of step after drawdown; positions cut in stages as risk budget is drawn down.
Outright trades only when price is too high or too low; otherwise curve spreads; stage out in spikes.
decision_process.why: Choose the trade structure that solves the problem.

decision_process.practice: Sell into spikes where final move is margin stress; accept de-risking and re-risking repeatedly on global risk-off days (Liberation Day).
decision_process.why: Noise around a theme does not mean the theme is wrong.

decision_process.practice: Be positioned for rare distortions and grind a decent return in quiet years.
decision_process.why: Entering after the move is late.

decision_process.practice: Physical trading arm disbanded in 2014-17 for poor margins and high counterparty credit risk.

speakers.evidence_style: First-hand trading stories and a 20-year track record; analogy to career experience; few quantified tests.

current_views.view: Pivoting to electrification metals (copper, aluminium, lithium) because supply and demand are harder to adjust; other commodities look well supplied.
current_views.reasoning: Data centres, EVs, China trucks; electrification pace is the swing factor.

current_views.view: Oil near $55 is similar to 2005 levels because of shale innovation; commodities generally are disappointing as long-run stores of value.
Fund not on copper's 2024 rally because cash basis did not follow; remained patient.

worldview_premises.premise: When an exchange cancels trades in a squeeze (LME nickel), the stated reason is protecting the clearing house but the effect is to bail out the distressed side.
Fellow traders talk their book, so views must be weighed against physical facts.
Regional gas prices can decouple: Henry Hub stayed quiet while LNG rose when Europe competed with China after Ukraine.

disagreements.topic: Risk leash: single-team fund vs multi-manager platform

positions.speaker: Doug King
positions.position: A single-team fund can sit through noise around a long-term supply-demand theme, while multi-manager platforms put commodity PMs on tight drawdown leashes (out after a few failures within months).

positions.speaker: Doug King (own fund)
positions.position: Still must cut and rebuild positions repeatedly on global risk-off days and has stringent risk processes.

gaps_and_conflicts.issue: Correction applied: the ICE cocoa margin squeeze belongs to Seibert; the cotton merchants wiped out by margin calls is King's story (C07-X1).

The fund's volatility target and size discipline are said to prevent holding full size on big winners, yet the fund claims to want to be positioned for rocket-ship moves; the tension is acknowledged only indirectly.
Fund performance claims (60% in 2014) and 'top performing hedge fund of the year' are self-reported.
No quantified rule for what counts as a 'full carry' or 'supply-demand story' worth risk; judgment-based.
Claim that precious metals are not physical supply-demand driven is not supported; the host jokes about silver.

forward_looking_inputs: (reader) Inputs King says lead prices: cash-futures basis and physical follow-through (weeks to months), storage levels and curve shape (carry vs inverse), OPEC supply decisions and shale growth against global GDP growth (months), electrification demand for copper, aluminium and lithium (years), exchange margin and limit rules at extremes (days). Reason: commodities are cyclical, ended by innovation; real tightness shows in cash.
reader_inferences: (reader) King is a discretionary fundamental trader whose edge is judged by cash-market confirmation, which could be tested as a basis-confirmation filter on futures trends.
(reader) His volatility targeting explicitly caps participation in the fattest tails, so his return stream differs from trend followers.
(reader) The strategy is built around waiting for distortions; years of idleness are by design.
